ending:
Jake remains at the Malefic Order's academy on Primordial 4. He has unrestricted access to its lessons and begins repairing the narrow theoretical base revealed by his entrance examination, with neurotoxins and Soulflames among his new interests. His false identity conceals most of his records and his status as Villy's Chosen, but his bloodline remains visible. A red-dragon faction has already identified him as a valuable new-universe bloodline bearer and opened a channel for future recruitment.

Mira remains contract-bound to Jake because release inside the Order would expose her to greater danger. Jake refuses to treat her as property, gives her broad lesson and travel permissions, and encourages her to choose a future that might eventually help her enslaved family. Reika studies separately with the Noboru Clan contingent, while Miranda leads Haven on Earth and completes a powerful ritual circle. Sylphie returns from an Altmar evaluation with a medal. The Fallen King continues independently while his true soul remains tied to Jake's mask. Eternal Hunger is contained but still capable of pressuring Jake, and William's monster-supported investigation remains unresolved.
in_short: After returning from the Yalsten treasure hunt, Jake reunites with family, helps Haven profit from a system auction, and restores the Fallen King from his mask. His attempt to forge a stronger cursed weapon causes the worldwide Great Famine, but he seals the curse within his soul and creates Eternal Hunger. He then survives a disastrous encounter with a C-grade hive defender, strengthens Haven's alliances, and leaves Earth for the revived Malefic Order. Training lets him falsify most of his visible records, though not his bloodline. At the Order academy, Jake's entrance tests expose both exceptional talent and major gaps in his alchemical education. A historical vision of Valdemar's victory over Villy gives him a true melee style. Jake is admitted with exceptional privileges and reluctantly accepts responsibility for Mira, an enslaved elf assigned to his household. He begins helping her develop an independent path while studying Soulflames and neurotoxins. A dragonflight detects his bloodline and attempts to recruit him, leaving his identity and inherited power under growing scrutiny.

recaps.text: Previously: Jake Thayne became a powerful hunter, alchemist, and the Malefic Viper's Chosen while helping establish Haven on newly integrated Earth. His closest allies include Haven's leader Miranda, the merchant Sultan, the inventor Arnold, his hawk companion Sylphie, and his brother Caleb, who leads the Court of Shadows. Jake's rivalry with the Sword Saint culminated in a damaging duel during the Yalsten treasure hunt, leaving possession of a blood legacy disputed between them. The hunt also gave Jake dangerous materials and obligations, including a promise connected to the vampire lineage Nalkar, the cursed Root of Yalsten's Eternal Resentment, and a mask containing a surviving consciousness. Casper, a Risen curse specialist, remains one of the few people qualified to advise him about such items. With the treasure hunt over, Jake is returning to family and Haven while considering how to develop his alchemy, settle unfinished bargains, and eventually visit the Malefic Order.

Jake travels toward Caleb while Villy explains the history of vampires and the surviving Nalkar lineage. At the Court of Shadows, William has already penetrated the hidden faction's defenses, questioned Caleb's family, and defeated pursuing assassins without killing them. Caleb discovers that William spent years in Nevermore and suspects a powerful monster enabled his return. William later meets a plane-shifting jellyfish that supplies his transport network and sets out for Sanct Domo to investigate Jake's past.

Jake reaches the Court's public decoy city, finds its concealed headquarters, and reunites with Caleb and their family. He meets his infant nephew Adam and helps Caleb expose recruits to controlled pressure so they can build resistance. Caleb also shows him an Umbral Lotus growing around the Court's pylon and gives him three ancient leaves for future neurotoxin work.

A system auction then opens for treasure-hunt participants. Jake joins Miranda, Sultan, Sylphie, Arnold, and Neil to sort Haven's haul. They retain practical defenses and alchemical materials, sell less useful treasures, and keep the dangerous Root of Yalsten's Eternal Resentment until Casper can assess it. Sultan takes charge of Jake's listings and bids as the auction begins.

The auction gives Jake a private booth, where he delegates trading to Sultan and spends much of the event making potions. His sales produce an enormous credit balance. He negotiates with the Sword Saint over the disputed blood legacy, agreeing to exchange selected Yalsten artifacts for continuing access while both men publicly call their duel a tie.

Jake acquires replacement armor, cursed bracers, a blood-focused dagger, a renewable quiver, and other useful materials. Arnold buys a damaged Yalsten transport pod for repair. When Casper examines Jake's cursed scimitar, he identifies a hunger-based sin curse that could eventually alter or consume its wielder. Casper warns Jake against combining it with the cursed root and an ancient weapon, but Jake retains the materials.

The auction's restricted bonus round includes the most valuable prizes. Caleb obtains the Heart of Darkness, Casper wins a dungeon core, and Jake purchases the Gift of Wind for Sylphie. She consumes it and falls into a restorative sleep. Jake finally gains a soulbound bow suited to an apex hunter. At the request of the consciousness in his mask, he spends heavily on Soul Renewal, a unique item that even Villy cannot clearly interpret. The auction ends with Jake planning several long-delayed projects.

Jake returns to Haven after the auction. Sultan receives the event's highest merchant title, while Villy confirms that Sylphie's Gift of Wind may reshape her development. Jake prepares an underground alchemy complex, assisted by Hank and Arnold, and establishes a renewable supply of serene water. Villy warns that Jake's planned curse ritual will create an intense urge to kill and advises him to perform it far from people.

Over the following months, Jake rebuilds his potion supply, improves his attributes, and finalizes his ritual plan. Sylphie wakes with a changed connection to wind, and Reika prepares to bring a Noboru Clan alchemical delegation to Haven. Jake then travels to the Insect Plains and pours Soul Renewal onto his mask.

The restored being is the Fallen King, the same King of the Forest who served as Jake's final tutorial foe. A fragment of his soul survived within the mask and recovered by drawing on Jake's soul-linked mana. The bond now ties the King's life to Jake, while his true soul remains in the mask. They reject a master-servant relationship, fight to an endurance stalemate, and agree to cooperate while seeking a safe way to separate. The Fallen King departs independently after giving Jake temporary protection against soul influence.

Jake transfers the hunger curse from his scimitar into an ancient weapon and draws the Root of Yalsten's Eternal Resentment into the ritual. When the Fallen King's temporary soul protection expires, the curse overwhelms him and drives him through a termite hive in search of life energy. The effect spreads worldwide, emptying food stores and causing mass hunger even in major settlements.

Jake reinforces the failing weapon with a Nalkar Vampire Heart and an alchemical catalyst, then retreats into his soul space to regain control. After eighteen days of transmutation, the global hunger returns to him as a curse manifestation. Jake binds it rather than allowing it to replace his identity and completes the mythical soulbound weapon Eternal Hunger. The crisis ends after more than three weeks and becomes known as the Great Famine, though its cause remains hidden. Eternal Hunger can drain many forms of energy and capture the souls of Jake's kills, but its appetite continues to pressure him.

Jake rejects further curse specialization and instead gains a soul-ritual skill. He pushes deeper into the termite hive, kills several D-grade queens, and attacks a C-grade hive queen. A combat-specialized hive king appears and nearly kills him within seconds. Jake escapes only by teleporting away and hiding underground with catastrophic injuries.

Jake remains hidden until his wounds heal, developing an improved arcane stealth skill that lets him mimic the surrounding tunnels. He escapes the hive and concludes that its deeper castes may become a planetary threat. In Haven, Miranda, Sultan, Roman, Felicia, and Lillian spare an intelligent undergrowth cave troll and its young during a dungeon expedition. Sultan relocates the family, and Jake offers the adult troll a place as caretaker of a new life-affinity garden.

Arnold studies Jake's cracked Altmar cauldron and discovers a rune that can restore it through repeated infusions of Jake's soul energies. He also finds sealed potential in Jake's storage necklace, though upgrading it will require additional expertise. Chris completes a monument designed as a gateway to the Malefic Order.

Reika arrives with a Noboru Clan delegation seeking alchemical exchange and stronger ties with Haven. Jake states that intelligent non-humans may live in the city if they follow its rules, despite the political resistance this policy may cause. He repairs his cauldron fully and spends three weeks sharing alchemical knowledge with the visitors. When Villy announces that the gateway is ready, Jake leaves Earth through it for secret training.

Jake reaches Primordial 4, where Villy trains him to control Shroud of the Primordial. The blessing already hides his records and karmic trail, but Jake must learn to decide what an observer sees. Villy repeatedly brings him near death under accelerated time so he can sense the shroud responding to scrutiny. Jake eventually develops an adaptive method that alters each incoming Identify attempt rather than relying on fixed false records.

After thirteen subjective years, Jake can display a fabricated race, level, blessing, and religious status. The shroud cannot conceal his bloodline, leaving him vulnerable to detection and unwanted attention. During this period, the Sword Saint accepts a blessing from the human time primordial and gains Weight of Time, strengthening the lasting record of his actions.

Jake briefly returns to Earth, authorizes a link between Haven and Sanct Domo, visits family, and invites Reika and eight other Noboru Clan alchemists to the Order academy. Miranda and Sylphie remain behind. On Primordial 4, an expired Nalkar token fails to pay for entry but may still be redeemed for compensation. Meanwhile, Villy publicly announces his return to more than five hundred gods and begins rebuilding his Order. His many newly blessed candidates also help conceal Jake's exceptional status.

Jake and the Noboru contingent enter the academy's placement process. Each applicant faces an individual dungeon whose performance determines benefits. Jake's examination begins with alchemy. He excels at identifying herbs and controlling mana, but the evaluator exposes how narrow and self-focused his practical experience is. His poison and potion work is potent yet limited, and his habit of forcing flawed energy out of creations wastes material. After reflecting on this criticism, he performs unevenly in transmutation before producing a powerful curse-bound weapon from the test materials. A month-long focus trial confirms his ability to sustain a ritual.

The combat examination better suits him. Jake clears escalating groups with bare hands, mental pressure, poison, archery, and Arcane Awakening. He defeats a coordinated five-person party by breaking its soul restraint and eliminating its healer first, then kills a level-186 manticore. The judges deem his performance exceptional and offer an optional eighth test.

Jake accepts a one-hour challenge against a two-headed incarnation of the Lord Protector, a level-160 hydra. His opening arrow barrage fails because the creature consumes mana-based attacks, absorbs their poison, and returns his magic. The hydra locates him and forces a direct confrontation in a highly unfavorable matchup.

Jake learns that the Lord Protector can consume his energy attacks but not ordinary physical blows, so he switches to melee. The hydra compresses its body into a faster, tougher form and overwhelms him. At the point of defeat, a childhood memory leads Jake into a historical record from Villy's path.

The record shows the Malefic Viper as an S-grade dragon fighting an injured human axe warrior over a sealed golden orb. Despite losing an arm and his weapon, the human breaks off one of the Viper's fangs, turns it into an axe, and wins. He is Valdemar, a future primordial. Repeated views of the battle let Jake study both fighters. Back in the trial, he develops Fangs of Man, a melee style that temporarily integrates compatible weapons with his soul shape, and upgrades his venom skill so toxins can flow through anything he treats as part of his weaponry. Time expires before he defeats the hydra, but he leaves with a viable future approach.

Jake receives an exceptional academy token and a replenishing petrifying venom reward. Villy explains that Valdemar's victory broke his former belief in innate monster superiority. Reika earns a lower placement and accepts criticism of her rigid alchemical method. Jake is formally admitted to the academy.

Academy entrants exchange their placement rewards for Order tokens that control identity, travel, contracts, and housing. Mira, an elf enslaved after her clan's defeat and trained in toxins and service, is assigned as the permanent steward and property of an important new entrant. Jake discovers her kneeling in his private residence and immediately confronts Villy.

Villy explains that the Order routinely uses slavery contracts to secure loyalty and secrecy, and that Mira receives protection through Jake's status. Jake wants to free her, but an openly released former Order slave would face grave danger and she now knows sensitive details about him. Given the choice, Mira asks to remain under his protection as the safest available course. Jake keeps the contract but rejects treating her as property, asks her not to call him master, and tries to give her room to act for herself.

Jake learns that his status as Villy's Chosen grants free access to every Order lesson. Mira demonstrates substantial knowledge of herbology and toxicology, prompting Jake to consider extending educational access to her. When she explains that generations of coercion have left her unable to identify personal desires, Jake gives her hundreds of lesson options and directs her to choose five for her own interest rather than his service.

Jake explores the academy's teaching while trying to broaden the theoretical foundation his entrance test found lacking. A combat-cauldron course proves poorly suited to him but introduces Soulflames. An A-grade dragon explains how willpower can make alchemical flame serve creation and destruction, and demonstrates an integrated Soulflame. Jake learns that these rare, semi-living treasures come from failed elemental births and can kill or cripple an incompatible alchemist. He postpones integration while studying safer fundamentals and neurotoxins.

Mira initially chooses lessons aimed only at becoming more useful. By imagining a better future for her enslaved father and siblings, she eventually selects subjects that could develop her own abilities. Jake grants her a subordinate token with broad permissions, and she begins attending lessons. In Haven, Miranda completes a powerful Yalsten-altar ritual circle, while Sylphie finishes an Altmar evaluation that cannot fully classify her transformed wind nature and returns with a medal.

A dragonflight investigates Jake after detecting signs of his bloodline. A young female dragonkin confirms the resonance and offers faction connections, which Jake declines while maintaining the name Hunter. Villy explains that a primordial-enforced treaty protects bloodline holders from abduction, enslavement, and reproductive coercion, but not recruitment or manipulation. The book closes with Jake pursuing neurotoxicology and Mira beginning to assert herself, both settling into sustained study at the Order.
